points: Q3 2026 will show whether the Q2 deal deferrals that management called 'deferral, not destruction' actually closed in the quarter; if they did not convert, revenue and bookings will miss and the short case gets stronger.

The Q2 report suggested full-year revenue growth guidance of 4-5%, so Q3 will reveal whether IBM is still on track or whether it must lower guidance; a guide-down or weak implied Q4 would undercut the premium valuation.
Q3 results will reveal if software and consulting — IBM's growth engines — are decelerating; slower growth there would weaken the AI/hybrid-cloud reacceleration narrative.
The print will show whether margins and free cash flow are holding up under revenue pressure; any compression would challenge a P/E near 19x and a PEG roughly 4x the computer industry median.
With FY1/FY2 EPS growth only about 6-7%, the stock needs accelerating growth to justify its premium PEG; anything less should pressure multiple compression.

Analysts have been cutting estimates into the print — 14 downward revisions versus 6 upward in the last 30 days and 90-day revenue estimates down 0.87% — so the bar is falling, not rising, which fits the short setup.
Peer prints from AMD and SMCI come after IBM, but IBM's own Q3 numbers and guidance will drive the trade over the next 50 days.
watch: Q3 revenue growth relative to the 4-5% full-year guide trajectory — below-guide or deceleration supports the short.
Software and consulting revenue growth — any slowdown supports the short.
Full-year revenue/EPS guidance — a cut or unchanged guidance with a weak implied Q4 supports the short.
Operating margin and free cash flow — compression or a miss supports the short.
